metadata.note: The Baltimore, Chesapeake and Atlantic corridor across Maryland's Eastern Shore, Claiborne (Eastern Bay steamer landing) - St. Michaels - Easton - Hurlock - Vienna - Salisbury - Berlin - Ocean City, 87.6 mi (Fowler line 53). One corridor, four operating companies: the Wicomico and Pocomoke (Salisbury - Berlin 1868, to Ocean City 1876/1881), the Baltimore and Eastern Shore (built Claiborne - Salisbury 1889-90, took in the W&P June 1890, sold 29 Aug 1894), the Baltimore, Chesapeake and Atlantic (30 Aug 1894 - 29 Mar 1928; PRR stock control from 1902/1905, not a split) and the wholly PRR-owned Baltimore and Eastern (1928 - passenger trains ended 1933/34; freight only by 1951). Rail only - the Baltimore - Claiborne steamers and the Annapolis - Claiborne ferries are not drawn. Research report: research/branches/baltimore_chesapeake_and_atlantic_railway.txt.
sources: https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/delawareandmarylandrrs.pdf -- J. Fowler, Delaware & Maryland Railroads, Passenger Stations & Stops, line 53 (BC&A) and 51 (B&E)

metadata.operator_split: Salisbury - Ocean City: W&P 1868-1890 (Salisbury - Berlin 1868, Berlin - Hammock Point 1876, the bay bridge 1881) | B&ES 1890-1894 | BC&A 1894-1928 | B&E 1928-1933. Claiborne - Easton: B&ES 1890-1894 | BC&A 1894-1924 [OPEN] | B&E excursion specials 1928 [ANCHOR], 1930-1931 [OPEN]. Easton - Hurlock: B&ES 1890-1894 | BC&A 1894-1928 | B&E 1928-1933 [OPEN]. Hurlock - Salisbury: B&ES 1890-1894 | BC&A 1894-1920 [OPEN] | B&E none confirmed. Splits share identical geometry. Transfer years (1890, 1894, 1928) are drawn under both companies, as the report's spans give them. PRR majority stock control (1902 / June 1905) is not a split. New colours, none used by any company in data/: Wicomico and Pocomoke #117332, Baltimore and Eastern Shore #8C8C15, Baltimore, Chesapeake and Atlantic #1D3DBF, Baltimore and Eastern #74158C. The Baltimore and Eastern gets its own colour, not the PRR's (#7B241C): it ran and advertised its trains under its own name (report ownership_split) - flagged for whoever owns the PRR palette.

segments.note: Wicomico and Pocomoke Railroad, Salisbury - Berlin, completed May 1868 (en.wikipedia citing Baltimore Sun 22 Apr 1868 - the Sun report was not read). Steam from the first train (eshore: 'first engine was a small wood-burning locomotive'); no animal era. The one primary-derived touchdown is the 1875 Official Guide (Fowler's 'y' letter at Pittsville, Whaleyville, St. Martin's and Berlin). Ends in 1890 only as an operator change: merged into the Baltimore and Eastern Shore in June 1890 (en.wikipedia citing Baltimore Sun 2 Jul 1890; the same article also says 'sold ... 1888' - conflict recorded, 1890 used); service continues as feature bes-salisbury-ocean-city. The 31 Mar 1870 extension to the Wicomico River wharves at Salisbury is freight/steamboat connection track and is not drawn. Headway is an estimate from the eshore article's undated 'two daily trips between Berlin and Salisbury'.

segments.note: Ocean City extension of the Wicomico and Pocomoke, built for the Atlantic Hotel resort: rails reached Hammock Point (West Ocean City) early 1875 and the hotel opened 4 Jul 1875 (en.wikipedia citing Baltimore Sun 28 Jan and 12 Jun 1875). Drawn from 1876, the year the Ocean City Bridge Co. pivot bridge was built (en.wikipedia citing Md. General Assembly 1876 / Baltimore Sun 16 Aug 1876) - the report's collapse of a 1875-vs-1876 start; whether trains ran to Hammock Point itself in 1875 is not established. Ends 1890 as an operator change (merged into the B&ES, see bes-salisbury-ocean-city). en.wikipedia's lead 'extended to Ocean City in 1870' contradicts its own body (construction began 1874) and is taken as an error. Headway estimated.

segments.note: Baltimore, Chesapeake and Atlantic (inc. 30 Aug 1894), west end to the Claiborne steamer landing for the BC&A's own Baltimore boats and, from 1912/1919, the Annapolis - Claiborne auto ferry (boats not drawn). PRR took majority stock in 1902 (qarrs.org: June 1905) - stock control only, the BC&A kept its own organisation and trains, so no split. Regular trains confirmed 1920-21 (Daily Banner, Cambridge: 6 Mar 1920 storm train Claiborne - Easton - Hurlock - Berlin; 13 Sep 1921 'the B. C. & A. train leaves Claiborne at 8.35 A. M.') and in the summer of 1924 (Worcester Democrat, weekly Jul-Sep 1924: Claiborne-Annapolis Ferry schedule in effect 28 Jun 1924, 'Connect with B. C. & A. trains at Claiborne for Easton, Hurlock, Salisbury, Ocean City'). [OPEN] END: 1924 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - en.wikipedia 'Claiborne, Maryland' (secondary, not verified) says the trains became a gasoline rail car after 1924 and the B&E had dropped regular service by 1928, but no source dates the last train. Do not extend without evidence. The 1924 ferry ad also lists buses from Claiborne; that is evidence of neither ending nor continuing. Headway estimated.
sources: Segment-level: report block [6] - Worcester Democrat 26 Jul 1924 p.4 (and weekly to 13 Sep 1924) for 1924; Daily Banner 6 Mar 1920 and 13 Sep 1921 p.3 for 1920-21; en.wikipedia BC&A for the 1894 start. End year is the last confirmed, not an end. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: BC&A, Easton (Claiborne Branch Jct, the PRR crossing) - Bethlehem - Preston - Ellwood - Hurlock: the section every through-train pattern used, via Vienna to Salisbury before c.1925 and (Fowler line 51 note) off at Hurlock onto the PRR via Seaford to Salisbury after c.1925 - the PRR track is not drawn here. Ends 1928 as an operator change: the BC&A was sold at foreclosure 29 Mar 1928 to Charles Carter for the PRR and reorganised as the Baltimore and Eastern, which ran on without a break (feature be-easton-hurlock). Headway estimated.

segments.note: BC&A, Hurlock - Rhodesdale - Vienna (Nanticoke River bridge) - Mardela Springs - Hebron - Salisbury. [OPEN] END: 1920 is the last CONFIRMED year (Daily Banner 6 Mar 1920: a storm-delayed BC&A train ran Claiborne - Hurlock - Berlin, which must have used this line since the Seaford routing came later), not a known end. Fowler line 51: 'Former route until c.1925' (through trains rerouted via the PRR at Seaford, approx); en.wikipedia BC&A: 'In 1932 cross peninsula travel was stopped when the Nanticoke trestle at Vienna was closed' - cited only to a railroad.net forum thread. SOURCE CONFLICT recorded, neither drawn. By Oct 1933 the B&E routed via Hurlock-Seaford-Salisbury (Smyrna Times 25 Oct 1933). Do not extend without evidence. No B&E-era passenger year is confirmed on this section, so it has no 1928+ feature. Freight continued: the 1952 Official Guide lists Preston - Vienna and West Ocean City - Hebron freight only, so Vienna - Hebron was gone by 1951. Headway estimated.

segments.note: Baltimore and Eastern Railroad (1928, wholly PRR-owned, run and advertised under its own name). 1928-33 B&E trains ran Love Point (Baltimore ferry) - Queen Anne - (PRR) Easton - here - Hurlock - (PRR) Seaford - Salisbury - Ocean City (Smyrna Times 25 Oct 1933); only this section is BC&A track - the Love Point line and the PRR pieces are not drawn in this layer. [OPEN] END: service is certain to Aug 1933; after the 23 Aug 1933 storm nothing ran to Ocean City, and the Md. PSC allowed withdrawal of Easton - Ocean City passenger service in July 1934 (Worcester Democrat 13 Jul 1934; replacement Love Point - Easton - Oxford service from 15 Jul 1934 does not use this section). Whether trains actually ran here Aug 1933 - Jul 1934 is only implied by the PSC case, so 1933 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end. Do not extend to 1934 without a 1934 timetable or report. Freight continued (1952 Official Guide: Preston - Vienna freight only; Hurlock - Preston later Maryland & Delaware RR). Headway estimated.
sources: Segment-level: report block [10] - Smyrna Times 25 Oct 1933 p.7 (route and Aug 1933 storm), Worcester Democrat 13 Jul 1934 p.13 (PSC withdrawal), en.wikipedia BC&A (1928 sale). End year is the last confirmed, not an end. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Baltimore and Eastern, Salisbury - Berlin - Ocean City, reached from Hurlock over the PRR via Seaford. Ends 1933: the storm of 23 Aug 1933 washed away the Sinepuxent Bay bridge and 'the railroad company has completely abandoned passenger train service to Ocean City' (Smyrna Times 25 Oct 1933); the PSC formally allowed withdrawal in July 1934 (Worcester Democrat 13 Jul 1934). Whether any passenger train ran Salisbury - Berlin after the storm is unknown and none is drawn. The bridge was never rebuilt; a freight station was set up at West Ocean City, and the 1952 Official Guide lists West Ocean City - Hebron freight only. Also carried WB&A-connecting Sunday excursion specials from Claiborne in 1928-31 (see be-claiborne-easton-excursions). Headway estimated.
sources: Segment-level: report block [11] - Smyrna Times 25 Oct 1933 p.7, Worcester Democrat 13 Jul 1934 p.13, Evening Star 2 Aug 1931 p.21 (1931 special). Headway not sourced.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] 1928: the one proven season of the first B&E summer, Evening Star 21 Jul 1928 p.3 - WB&A special for Sunday 22 Jul 1928 'connecting with non-stop train at Claiborne for Ocean City (Arriving Ocean City 12:30 noon)'. Service certainly ran wider than one year both ways (1929 not found, not searched exhaustively), but no other year is confirmed; do not close the 1929 gap without a 1929 ad. Summer Sunday excursion specials only - the WB&A ran a special Washington - Annapolis ferry wharf, the ferry crossed to Claiborne, and a B&E 'non-stop train at Claiborne for Ocean City' ran out about 12:30 noon and back from Ocean City at 4:15 P.M. Counts under Rule 1 as one-off passenger specials. Regular B&E service on Claiborne - Easton after 1928 is NOT established (en.wikipedia 'Claiborne, Maryland' says the B&E had dropped it by 1928), so only the advertised seasons are drawn. The specials' route between Hurlock and Salisbury (Vienna or Seaford) is not stated. Headway is a placeholder for one train each way on a handful of Sundays.
sources: Segment-level: report block [12] - Evening Star 21 Jul 1928 p.3. Headway not sourced (placeholder).
